# Parse all notes to extract date and habit values
import re

# Get habit order from the first note (note 468)
first_note = all_notes[0]
habit_order = []
for line in first_note['content'].split('\n'):
    line = line.strip()
    if line and not line.startswith('#') and ': ' in line:
        habit = line.split(': ')[0].strip()
        habit_order.append(habit)
print("Habit order:", habit_order)

# Parse all notes
parsed_notes = []
for note in all_notes:
    # Extract date from title: "Habit Tracking Log for 2023-05-17"
    m = re.search(r'(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})', note['title'])
    if not m:
        print(f"Warning: no date in title for note {note['note_id']}")
        continue
    date = m.group(1)
    habits = {}
    for line in note['content'].split('\n'):
        line = line.strip()
        if line and not line.startswith('#') and ': ' in line:
            habit, value = line.split(': ', 1)
            habits[habit.strip()] = value.strip().lower()
    parsed_notes.append({'date': date, 'habits': habits})

# Sort by date ascending
parsed_notes.sort(key=lambda x: x['date'])
print(f"Parsed {len(parsed_notes)} notes, first date: {parsed_notes[0]['date']}, last date: {parsed_notes[-1]['date']}")
